title: Solaris Therapeutics POC - weekly bench compare: latency & throughput
summary: Weekly POC check-in to review lab benchmarks vs customer's incumbent provider. Focus on tail latency at 95/99p, steady-state throughput, routing fallbacks. SE presented quantization + batching tunings; customer raised VPC/KMS requirements and asked for SOC2 docs. Agreed to run a 12-hour sustained load test and share logs + latency histograms. Next: Redwood to share perf runbook and pricing delta; customer to provide realistic traffic trace and confirm SLA needs.
topics: next steps: sustained load test and artifacts to exchange
action_items: Alicia Ramos | Send perf runbook + quantization tuning notes | 2026-05-01
Devon Park | Kick off 12-hour sustained load run on Redwood Dedicated variant, attach histograms | 2026-04-30
Maya Chen | Provide 24h representative traffic trace & top prompt templates | 2026-04-30
Tom Li | Confirm required latency SLOs (95p/99p) and procurement window | 2026-05-04
Jordan Weiss | Share SOC2/ISO whitepaper link and KMS integration doc | 2026-04-29
next_steps: Run sustained 12-hour throughput test against Redwood Dedicated + quantized model and compare to incumbent averages
Share latency histograms and raw logs for 95p/99p windows
Customer to validate VPC/KMS constraints and provide firewall egress rules
Alicia to send preliminary pricing delta for dedicated capacity and expected unit-cost improvements
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-28 14:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Alicia, Devon, Jordan (Redwood); Tom, Maya, Priya, Sam (Solaris)

[00:00] Alicia Ramos (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:08] Tom Li (CTO): Tom here.
[00:10] Maya Chen (SRE): Maya.
[00:12] Priya Singh (Lead ML Eng): Priya.
[00:14] Sam Ortiz (Infra): Sam.
[00:16] Alicia Ramos (AE): Great. On our side Alicia, Devon and Jordan. The goal today is a bench compare and triage of the tail latency gaps you saw last week. Devon, you want to lead?
[00:28] Devon Park (SE): Sure. Quick context, we re-ran the 1k concurrent sessions scenario you sent, same prompt mix, looked at two variants: Hosted (Redwood API) and Dedicated with int8 quant and batching tweaks. Baseline is your incumbent provider snapshot from 4/20.
[00:45] Priya Singh (Lead ML Eng): quick note, the incumbent run has a warm-up artifact, we tried to match warm caches but not perfect.
[00:51] Devon Park (SE): yeah we saw that; we added a 30-minute warm-up and pre-populated KV cache to be fair.
[00:57] Devon Park (SE): Results: median token latency is comparable +- 5ms, 95th is within 10-20ms for 128 token truncation, but 99th spikes on our dedicated at certain moments to ~280ms vs incumbent 190ms. Throughput steady-state we hit 780 RPS on the Dedicated config vs 720 RPS for the incumbent, so better throughput but worse tail in bursts.
[01:32] Tom Li (CTO): Why is 99p worse if throughput is higher? sounds like queuing or long GC pauses?
[01:40] Devon Park (SE): Likely queuing and also batching heuristics. At high concurrency our continuous-batcher sometimes creates larger micro-batches which increases token latency for a small subset. We tuned the batch window down to reduce that but it decreases overall throughput. There is a tradeoff.
[02:05] Maya Chen (SRE): Can you share batch-size distribution? the histogram would help.
[02:10] Devon Park (SE): Yes, we'll attach. We saw a bimodal batch size during traffic spikes — some requests got 1-2 token micro-batches, others 32+ tokens. That mismatch is what's pushing the tail.
[02:25] Priya Singh (Lead ML Eng): also curious about KV cache eviction timing - did you hit cache misses that caused recompute?
[02:31] Devon Park (SE): Good catch. We saw periodic cache churn when sequence lengths varied — our default TTL was 45 minutes for that run, but with your prompts mixing long/short sequences there were misses. Increasing MAX cache entries helped. We'll test variant with longer TTL.
[02:50] Sam Ortiz (Infra): For Dedicated are you using our VPC peering or the private deployment? we need firewall and egress details for the sustained run.
[02:58] Jordan Weiss (CSM): We can do both depending on your preference — the Dedicated pool can be peered into your VPC; private on-prem would be a separate engagement. For the test we'll set up a peered subnet and share allowed IPs.
[03:15] Tom Li (CTO): Security stuff: we need KMS integration and audit logs for any PII requests. Is Redwood's KMS HSM-backed?
[03:24] Jordan Weiss (CSM): We support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS and HSM-backed integrations for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and rotation. I'll drop the SOC2 and KMS doc links after the call.
[03:38] Devon Park (SE): Back to perf, one more variable: quantization profile. Our int8 path improved throughput but slightly increases per-token compute variance on longer sequences. We have a hybrid quant profile that leaves attention layers in fp16 which smooths the 99p but reduces throughput ~6%.
[04:00] Priya Singh (Lead ML Eng): so we can tune to favor lower tail or higher throughput; what's the lift for the hybrid quant?
[04:07] Devon Park (SE): In our small runs it lowered the 99p from 280ms to ~210ms and throughput drops from 780 to ~730 RPS.
[04:17] Tom Li (CTO): that's interesting — 210ms 99p is close to incumbent but still a bit higher. Can we get histograms for token counts and latencies per prompt type?
[04:26] Devon Park (SE): yes will attach per-prompt histograms and raw percentiles.
[04:30] Alicia Ramos (AE): Pricing question — Jordan, any preliminary guidance how dedicated pricing vs hosted would look for their commit size?
[04:37] Jordan Weiss (CSM): We estimated a dedicated slot for this workload at about 18% lower unit token cost vs hosted at their expected QPS, but committed pricing and longer-term quantization tuning could push to ~25% savings. We'll put numbers in a short spreadsheet.
[04:55] Maya Chen (SRE): On the sustained run, we want to see impact of cold starts and rolling restarts, can you simulate a node reboot?
[05:03] Devon Park (SE): We can instrument a rolling restart mid-run and capture tail impact; we recommend doing a scheduled rolling-restart test to validate graceful fallback and routing.
[05:13] Priya Singh (Lead ML Eng): About routing — when you fallback from Dedicated to Hosted variant how do you keep model version parity? we need consistent outputs for evaluation.
[05:22] Devon Park (SE): We maintain model pinning across variants; fallback points map to compatible model family and quant profile, and we log variant-id in the response for traceability. Small diffs can exist due to quantization but we keep an eval harness to verify drift.
[05:37] Tom Li (CTO): Cool. Also, can Redwood enforce region affinity? some workloads must stay in eu-central.
[05:45] Jordan Weiss (CSM): Yes, routing policies include region affinity and tiers; we can ensure traffic remains in the EU region and fallback within region only.
[05:55] Sam Ortiz (Infra): Network question: we'll need a list of IP ranges and conns to allow outbound, don't assume dynamic ephemeral ports are open by default.
[06:05] Alicia Ramos (AE): We'll send an infra checklist.
[06:09] Priya Singh (Lead ML Eng): Any observed model-quality regressions after quant? we saw some token-prob shifts in a couple of prompts last week.
[06:16] Devon Park (SE): We ran evals on your test set: Rouge and BERTScore within <1% delta for hybrid; full int8 had a couple of edge cases under 2-3% but nothing catastrophic. We'll include sampling where outputs diverged.
[06:33] Tom Li (CTO): For the sustained run, what telemetry do you need from our side?
[06:36] Devon Park (SE): The traffic trace, prompt templates, and a list of heavy keys we should prewarm in KV cache. Also SLO targets for 95/99 so we can aim for the exact window.
[06:47] Priya Singh (Lead ML Eng): We'll provide a 24-hour trace with headers stripped.
[06:50] Maya Chen (SRE): Also include error patterns — when you say 99p spike was there an associated CPU/GPU saturation?
[06:56] Devon Park (SE): Our metrics show GPU utilization peaked but not saturated, the tail correlated to micro-batch contention.
[07:04] Jordan Weiss (CSM): A quick logistic: we'll schedule the sustained 12-hour run overnight to match your low-traffic window — target start 04/30 01:00 UTC. Does that work?
[07:12] Tom Li (CTO): yes works for us.
[07:15] Alicia Ramos (AE): Great. Any blockers on the SOC2/KMS side?
[07:19] Tom Li (CTO): Need the docs and an initial attestation for procurement.
[07:22] Jordan Weiss (CSM): I'll email the pack by EOD tomorrow.
[07:26] Priya Singh (Lead ML Eng): One more thing — can you include a sample of the log schema and the latency histogram format so we can ingest into Splunk?
[07:34] Devon Park (SE): Yep, JSON schema and histogram buckets included in the run artifacts.
[07:37] Alicia Ramos (AE): Recap please, Devon?
[07:41] Devon Park (SE): Recap: run 12-hour sustained test on 4/30 01:00 UTC against Dedicated quantized + hybrid variants, include rolling-restart test, collect latency histograms and per-prompt breakdowns, Redwood to push perf runbook and pricing delta, Solaris to provide 24h traffic trace and confirm SLOs.
[07:58] Tom Li (CTO): sounds good.
[08:00] Maya Chen (SRE): thanks all.
[08:02] Alicia Ramos (AE): We'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the test. Appreciate the time.
[08:07] (call ends)
